newsitem.title: BELGIUM: OLO SUPPLY TO PROMPT SWITCH IN 5-YR BENCHMARK.
newsitem.headline: OLO SUPPLY TO PROMPT SWITCH IN 5-YR BENCHMARK.

text.p: Monday's Belgian linear bond (OLO) auction may encourage more players to switch to OLO 10 (June 25, 2002) as their five-year benchmark, traders said on Friday.
Monday will be the first time in four years OLO 10 has been sold at a regular Treasury auction.

OLO 10, which was last month offered in an exchange auction, is already a highly liquid issue, with more than 330 billion francs outstanding, a Treasury official said. "The market wants this to be the new benchmark."
OLO 10 yielded 4.63 percent late on Friday.
"Maybe I'll change next week. We'll see. It's a question of liquidity," one trader said. Others said they would wait and see if the Treasury started a new five-year line later in the year.

Many houses presently use OLO 7 (9.00 pct, June 2001) as their benchmark, a bond which is also highly liquid with more than 308 billion francs outstanding. This bond is used by J.P. Morgan on its five-year benchmark page.
Dealers said the prospect of Monday's auction could further pressure prices. The market has been struggling all week to digest 60 billion francs of supply from an exchange auction.
The benchmark 10-year OLO 26 (6.25 pct, March 2007) -- which is also being auctioned on Monday -- slipped on Friday, with the spread over equivalent Bunds edging out to 10 basis points.
OLO 26 yielded 5.62 percent in late trade, up from 5.61 on Thursday, but down from 5.64 earlier in a day whose tone was set by overnight weakness in U.S. Treasuries.
